feedback.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $f(x)=7{x}^{2}-2$ at the point $(2,26)$ intersects the $y$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=7{x}^{2}-2.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{2}-2)=14x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(2)=14(2)=28.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(26) & =28(x-2) \\ y & =28x-56+26 \\ y & =28x-30.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $y$-axis, we set $x=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =28(0)-30 \\ y & =-30\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $(0,-30).$
